title: WEVSR: Video Diffusion Generators for Real-World Video Super‑Resolution with Wavelet-Enhanced VAE Encoder
claim: Compared to existing methods, ours restores realistic, artifact-free detail from degraded inputs, shown on zoomed crops.
layout: 2 columns, large frames above, zoomed crop comparisons below, red boxes link them
description: The figure has two columns, one for a real-world video example and one for a synthetic example. Each column has a large frame at the top with a vertical slider. The left side of the slider shows the low-quality input (VideoLQ on the left, UDM10 on the right) and the right side shows the output labeled 'SR (Ours)'. The left scene is a street crowd with children and strollers. The right scene is a man drinking in a cafe, with a chalkboard and a plant. Small red boxes mark regions of interest: a face on the left, a potted plant on the right. Below each frame is a row of zoomed crops of that region. The crops come from RealViFormer, STAR, SeedVR2 and Ours on the left, and from RealViFormer, SeedVR2 and Ours on the right. Baselines show distorted faces and blurry foliage, and ours looks sharper and more natural. White labels on translucent boxes name each result.
caption: Visualization comparisons on both real-world and synthetic low-resolution videos. Compared to the state-of-the-art VSR
abstract: Recent advances in video diffusion models have demonstrated remarkable generative capability, yet adapting these large pretrained text-to-video (T2V) models to video super‑resolution (VSR) typically encounters challenges, such as artifacts introduced by complex degradations in real-world scenarios and compromised fidelity due to the strong generative capacity of the powerful T2V models. We present WEVSR, a novel approach that adapts a pretrained flow-matching video diffusion transformer to VSR. First, we design a task-oriented adaptation strategy that leverages timestep sampling and noise augmentation to enhance detail restoration while preserving structural stability. Second, we propose a lightweight multi-level discrete wavelet transform (DWT) front-end for the VAE encoder, injecting explicit frequency priors into the latent space without modifying the pretrained decoder. Extensive experiments across multiple VSR benchmarks demonstrate that WEVSR achieves state-of-the-art performance against existing approaches. Code and models will be released here.
